transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-25
Time: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 54m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE); Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE); Dr. Alice Monroe (SummitCare); Tom Reyes (SummitCare Eng Lead); Karen Lin (SummitCare Compliance)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Discussed quality evaluation plan for POC focusing on golden prompts, hallucination checks, regression tests, scoring approach and timelines. Action items listed.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone thanks for carving out time, uh i know schedules are busy so we'll jump in. quick round robin who we have?
[00:12] Dr. Alice Monroe: Alice here. thanks. very excited to see how Redwood can help with clinical summarization.
[00:17] Tom Reyes: Tom, engineering. we'll be owning the dataset provisioning and infra.
[00:21] Karen Lin: Karen from compliance - i'll track SOC2/PHI needs.
[00:25] Priya Nambiar: Priya, se at Redwood, i'll be running the benchmarks and helping with eval scripts.
[00:31] Jordan Lee: great. objective today:align on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, and the quality evaluation plan - golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination and format checks, scoring. also timelines for a pilot/POC.

[02:05] Tom Reyes: quick question on workload sizing - for our triage flow we expect about 15k user events per day peak, roughly 4M tokens/day. are you seeing that as heavy for a POC?
[02:18] Priya Nambiar: not necessarily, we can run a representative subset for the POC. for the baseline we'll ask for a stratified 2k de-identified records that reflect short/med/long notes. that'll let us estimate latency and token cost.
[02:32] Dr. Alice Monroe: okay 2k sounds doable if we strip PHI - we'll work with Tom on that.

[04:10] Jordan Lee: success criteria draft - quick readout: 1) Quality: on golden prompt set, >= 92% correctness score (details to come), hallucination rate < 2% on golden, format compliance >= 98% 2) Performance: 95th_pct latency < 1200ms on our baseline prompts 3) Cost: unit cost target less than your current $X per 1k tokens - we'll model it in pricing 4) Security: must meet SOC2 and ability to run in VPC/Private if needed.

[05:04] Karen Lin: can you clarify hallucination measurement? we need operationalizable metric - false clinical assertions flagged vs gold. also audit logs for every generation.
[05:20] Priya Nambiar: yes - plan is to include hallucination checks via a set of fact-check prompts and extraction tasks. for clinical assertions we use a combination of exact match & entity-level verification; each generation will be scored for unsupported assertions. we'll expose per-response flags and aggregate hallucination rate. logs retained per your retention policy - we can include those in the security pack.

[07:12] Dr. Alice Monroe: golden prompts - what do you mean by those specifically?
[07:18] Priya Nambiar: golden prompts are curated examples that cover the most critical behaviors: e.g., discharge summary condensation, risk-flag extraction, triage-suggester. we will work with your clinical SMEs to identify 40-60 golden prompts plus expected outputs. these are used for regression checks and acceptance.

[08:05] Tom Reyes: for regression tests, do you run them automatically per model update?
[08:10] Priya Nambiar: yes, we run the golden set as a regression suite on candidate model variants. we compare scoring across versions and measure drift. we'll also include random holdout sets from your data to check unseen cases.

[09:01] Jordan Lee: scoring approach proposal - simple weighted rubric: correctness (50%), hallucination penalty (30%), format/structure compliance (15%), latency penalty (5%). correctness is multi-metric: clinical entity match (40% of correctness), instruction following and safety checks (60% of correctness). final score threshold for acceptance: >= 85% on weighted score and no single critical test failing.

[10:35] Dr. Alice Monroe: will you provide breakdown per metric so we can see details?
[10:38] Priya Nambiar: absolutely - the benchmark CSV includes per-prompt correctness, hallucination flag, format pass/fail, tokens, latency. we also compute aggregated percentiles.

[12:00] Tom Reyes: what about hallucination detection automation? manual labeling for 2k records is heavy.
[12:07] Priya Nambiar: agreed - initial run uses a mix: automated heuristics + a small manual review sample. automated checks include knowledge footprint tests (does the answer reference facts present in input?), entity cross-checks, and a weak entailment model. then a clinical reviewer samples ~200 outputs for sanity and to calibrate thresholds.

[13:45] Jordan Lee: example acceptance workflow: week 0 - provide data & golden prompts; week 1 - Redwood runs baseline and returns CSV + dashboard; week 2 - joint benchmark session and iterate prompts; week 3-4 - run full regression suite on candidate configuration; week 4 - acceptance decision or extend to Private trial. timeline flexible but that's our usual cadence for a 4-6 week POC.

[15:10] Karen Lin: compliance question - if we need Private deployment, how do eval logs get handled? retention and KMS?
[15:18] Priya Nambiar: we support Private with customer-managed KMS, logs kept in your VPC, and we can ship the audit bundle. we'll share the security whitepaper and SOC2 artifacts.

[16:20] Dr. Alice Monroe: scoring - can we upweight hallucination for clinical-critical prompts? some prompts are safety-critical.

[16:28] Jordan Lee: yes we recommend per-prompt importance weights. golden prompts will be tagged by criticality and we compute a weighted acceptance score where critical prompts are penalized more for hallucinations. we'll include that in the draft eval plan.

[17:45] Tom Reyes: workload sizing for peak - you said batching & KV cache matter for cost/latency. can you outline what config we'd test?
[17:54] Priya Nambiar: for the POC we'll test three configs: Hosted baseline; Dedicated small (2 GPU pool) with batching tuned; and quantized model variant (if acceptable). We'll report tokens/sec, steady-state latency, and cost per 1k tokens for each. caching will be simulated by including repeated prefixes in the dataset to measure prefix hit rates.

[19:05] Jordan Lee: benchmarks to run: 1) Golden prompt pass/fail and weighted score 2) Regression on holdout 3) Hallucination sampling 4) Format validation (JSON schema adherence, length constraints) 5) Throughput & 95/99 pctl latency 6) Cost modeling 7) Safety tests (prompt injections, red-team vectors).

[21:30] Dr. Alice Monroe: format checks - we need strict JSON outputs for downstream parsers. what's the tolerance for minor format deviations?
[21:37] Priya Nambiar: we'll implement strict schema checks with a pass/fail per response. format compliance >= 98% is target; failures are logged with example traces. we can also auto-run repair heuristics but for acceptance we require schema passes.

[23:15] Tom Reyes: how will we measure hallucination rate numerically? what's a hallucination on an extraction task?
[23:22] Priya Nambiar: for extractions, hallucination = extracted entity not present or contradicted by source. we compute percent_hallucination = (num_responses_with_hallucinated_entities / total_responses) * 100. for summaries, we check for any incorrect clinical claim relative to input and flag. thresholds are configurable per prompt type.

[25:00] Jordan Lee: scoring examples - if correctness=90%, hallucination rate=3% (penalized), format compliance=99%, latency ok, weighted score may drop below acceptance because hallucination carries heavy penalty. we'll show sensitivity analysis in the CSV.

[27:12] Dr. Alice Monroe: any reference artifacts we should review?
[27:16] Jordan Lee: yes - i'll send the Redwood POC eval template (link: https://redwood.ai/poc-eval-template) and the benchmark script repo (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/poc-bench). also security pack link (internal): https://redwood.ai/security-pack.

[28:55] Tom Reyes: are there any notable caveats with model updates during POC? we don't want regression mid-test.
[29:02] Priya Nambiar: we will pin model versions for your POC and only test defined candidate configs. we run regression tests on any non-pinned update and will notify you before changes.

[30:30] Karen Lin: auditing: we need retention policy documented and ability to produce audit logs for specific timeframe.

[30:37] Jordan Lee: noted; will include retention options in the security packet.

[32:00] Priya Nambiar: on tooling - we'll provide a dashboard that shows per-prompt score breakdown, hallucination flags, per-model comparison, and a CSV export for your data team.

[33:40] Dr. Alice Monroe: can Redwood help craft the golden prompts? we don't have time to create a big set right now.

[33:45] Priya Nambiar: yes we'll co-curate - start with 20 key clinical-critical prompts from your team, Redwood adds 20-40 variations for coverage. we'll iterate during the first week.

[35:12] Jordan Lee: acceptance criteria recap: weighted score >=85%, hallucination on critical prompts = 0% tolerance for severe clinical contradictions, format pass >=98%, 95th latency target met, and security checklist completed. if any one critical item fails, we either extend or move to Private trial depending on root cause.

[36:50] Tom Reyes: logistics - we'll anonymize data and share S3 link. who should I grant access to?

[36:55] Jordan Lee: please grant access to priya@redwood.com and jordan@redwood.com; and include an IAM role for read-only.

[38:20] Karen Lin: i'll need the data handling playbook and DPA language for PHI in the POC.

[38:25] Jordan Lee: we'll attach the DPA and data handling docs with the security pack.

[40:00] Priya Nambiar: one more technical: for hallucination testing we also ask for a small ground-truth set where outputs are labeled as true/false for claims. even 200 labeled items goes a long way.

[41:10] Dr. Alice Monroe: okay we can prioritize 200 labeled cases from our clinical team.

[42:35] Jordan Lee: excellent. quick recap of next steps: Jordan will send the draft eval plan + links and pricing by 6/28; Tom to provide the data by 6/30; Priya to run baseline benchmarks and return CSV by 7/2; schedule joint benchmark session w/ infra for week of 7/6.

[44:00] Tom Reyes: sounds good. one last ask - can we see a cost/latency tradeoff chart for Dedicated vs Hosted?

[44:08] Priya Nambiar: yes we'll include a comparative matrix in the baseline report.

[45:30] Karen Lin: thanks all.

[45:35] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone - any other questions?

[45:40] Dr. Alice Monroe: none here. looking forward.

[45:45] Jordan Lee: great we'll follow up with the links and plan. talk soon.

End of transcript.

References mentioned: https://redwood.ai/poc-eval-template, https://github.com/redwood-inference/poc-bench, security pack link (internal)
